## Why This Is Asked
Tests non-branching bit-twiddling across a 128-bit value. The triple overlap trick scales beyond 64 bits.

## Key Concepts
- Wide integer bit shifts with zero fill
- Bitwise AND to intersect bit positions
- Non-branching return logic for 0/1 result

```c
unsigned hasThreeConsecutiveOnes128(uint128 x){
  uint128 t = x & (x>>1) & (x>>2);
  return t != 0;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of bitwise rotations, a common low-level operation, and handling edge cases when k wraps around 32 without using branches. It also demonstrates how to make shifts robust against k=0 or k=31.

- Bitwise rotation using shifts and OR
- Modulo wrapping using masking and two's complement tricks
- Avoiding undefined shifts for k=0

## Code Example
```javascript
function rotateLeft32(n, k) {
  k = k & 31;
  return ((n << k) | (n >>> ((-k) & 31))) >>> 0;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests a crisp bit-twiddling trick: constructing a mask anchored to the least significant set bit, plus proper zero handling.

## Key Concepts
- Isolating the LSB with n & -n
- Mask construction via (lsb<<1) - 1
- Edge-case handling for zero input

## Code Example
```javascript
function maskBelowLSB32(n) {
  const lsb = n & -n;
  return n === 0 ? 0 : (lsb << 1) - 1;
}
```
